notes.definition: An atom is a very small particle (radius about 1 × 10⁻¹⁰ m) made of a tiny, positively charged nucleus containing protons and neutrons, surrounded by negatively charged electrons at different distances from the nucleus.
explanation: Atoms are extremely small. A typical atom has a radius of about 1 × 10⁻¹⁰ m (0.1 nanometres). That means about ten million atoms placed side by side would stretch across just one millimetre. Everything around you, including your own body, is made of atoms.

At the centre of every atom is the nucleus. The nucleus contains protons, which have a positive charge, and neutrons, which have no charge. So the nucleus as a whole is positively charged. The nucleus is tiny compared with the whole atom: its radius is less than 1/10 000 of the radius of the atom. Even so, almost all of the mass of the atom is concentrated in the nucleus, because protons and neutrons are much heavier than electrons.

Around the nucleus are electrons, which are negatively charged and have a very small mass. The electrons are arranged at different distances from the nucleus, in energy levels (sometimes called shells). Most of the volume of an atom is empty space between the nucleus and the electrons.

The electron arrangement can change. If an electron absorbs electromagnetic radiation, it gains energy and moves to an energy level further from the nucleus (a higher energy level). If an electron falls back to an energy level closer to the nucleus (a lower energy level), it emits electromagnetic radiation. Only particular amounts of energy can be absorbed or emitted, because the energy levels are at fixed distances.

A useful way to picture the scale is to imagine the nucleus enlarged to the size of a pea in the centre of a football stadium. The electrons would be found around the outer stands, and nearly everything in between would be empty space. This is why the diagrams in textbooks are never drawn to scale.
keyFacts: The radius of an atom is about 1 × 10⁻¹⁰ m.
The nucleus contains protons (positive) and neutrons (no charge).
The nucleus is positively charged overall.
The radius of the nucleus is less than 1/10 000 of the radius of the atom.
Almost all of the mass of an atom is in the nucleus.
Electrons are negatively charged and arranged at different distances from the nucleus (energy levels).
Most of an atom is empty space.
Absorbing electromagnetic radiation moves an electron further from the nucleus (to a higher energy level).
Emitting electromagnetic radiation happens when an electron moves closer to the nucleus (to a lower energy level).

keyTerms.definition: The smallest part of an element; a nucleus surrounded by electrons, with a radius of about 1 × 10⁻¹⁰ m.
The tiny, positively charged centre of an atom, containing protons and neutrons and almost all of the mass.
A positively charged particle found in the nucleus.
An uncharged (neutral) particle found in the nucleus.
A very light, negatively charged particle found in energy levels around the nucleus.
A fixed distance from the nucleus at which electrons can be found; levels further out have higher energy.

workedExamples.title: Comparing the size of the nucleus and the atom
workedExamples.question: An atom has a radius of 1 × 10⁻¹⁰ m. Its nucleus has a radius that is 1/10 000 of this. Calculate the radius of the nucleus.
steps: Radius of nucleus = radius of atom ÷ 10 000.

workedExamples.title: A scale model of an atom
workedExamples.question: A student models a nucleus as a ball of radius 2 cm. The radius of the atom is 10 000 times the radius of the nucleus. Calculate the radius of the model atom in metres.
steps: Radius of model atom = 2 cm × 10 000 = 20 000 cm.

workedExamples.title: Converting atom size
workedExamples.question: Write 1 × 10⁻¹⁰ m in nanometres (1 nm = 1 × 10⁻⁹ m).

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think the electrons take up most of the mass of an atom because they fill most of its volume.
misconceptions.right: In fact electrons have a tiny mass. Almost all the mass is in the nucleus, which takes up only a tiny fraction of the volume.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think the nucleus is about half the size of the atom, as it looks in many diagrams.
misconceptions.right: In fact the radius of the nucleus is less than 1/10 000 of the radius of the atom. Diagrams are not to scale.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think neutrons are negatively charged, to balance the protons.
misconceptions.right: In fact neutrons have no charge. It is the electrons that balance the positive charge of the protons.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think an electron emits radiation when it moves further from the nucleus.
misconceptions.right: In fact moving further out needs energy, so radiation is absorbed. Radiation is emitted when an electron moves closer to the nucleus.

realWorld: Neon signs and street lights glow because electrons in excited atoms fall to lower energy levels and emit light of particular colours.
Fireworks get their colours from metal atoms whose electrons absorb energy and then emit visible light as they return to lower energy levels.
Scientists identify the elements in distant stars by studying the particular wavelengths of light their atoms absorb and emit.
examTips: Learn the two key sizes: atom radius about 1 × 10⁻¹⁰ m, and nucleus radius less than 1/10 000 of that (about 1 × 10⁻¹⁴ m).
When describing the nucleus, say what it contains (protons and neutrons) and its charge (positive). Both are often needed for full marks.
Link direction to absorption or emission carefully: further from the nucleus means radiation absorbed; closer to the nucleus means radiation emitted.
When dividing powers of ten, subtract the indices: 10⁻¹⁰ ÷ 10⁴ = 10⁻¹⁴. Check by estimating whether the answer should be bigger or smaller.
summary: Atoms are very small, with a radius of about 1 × 10⁻¹⁰ m.
The nucleus contains protons and neutrons and is positively charged.
The nucleus radius is less than 1/10 000 of the atom radius but holds almost all the mass.
Negative electrons are arranged in energy levels at different distances from the nucleus.
Absorbing EM radiation moves electrons further out; emitting EM radiation happens when they move closer.

questions.question: What is the approximate radius of an atom?
markScheme: 1 mark: 1 × 10⁻¹⁰ m
questions.explanation: Atoms have a radius of about 1 × 10⁻¹⁰ m. 1 × 10⁻¹⁴ m is roughly the size of a nucleus, and 1 × 10⁻⁶ m (a micrometre) is the size of a bacterium.

questions.question: Which particles are found in the nucleus of an atom?
markScheme: 1 mark: Protons and neutrons
questions.explanation: The nucleus contains protons and neutrons. Electrons are found in energy levels outside the nucleus. Most nuclei contain neutrons as well as protons.

questions.question: What is the charge on a neutron?
markScheme: 1 mark: No charge
questions.explanation: Neutrons are neutral. The negative charge in an atom comes from electrons, and the positive charge from protons.

questions.question: What is the overall charge of the nucleus?
markScheme: 1 mark: Positive
questions.explanation: The nucleus contains positive protons and neutral neutrons, so it is positive overall. Electron movement does not change the nucleus.

questions.question: Where is almost all of the mass of an atom found?
markScheme: 1 mark: In the nucleus
questions.explanation: Protons and neutrons are much more massive than electrons, and they are all in the nucleus. So almost all the mass is in the nucleus, even though it is tiny.

questions.question: How does the radius of the nucleus compare with the radius of the atom?
options: It is about half the radius of the atom
It is about 1/100 of the radius of the atom
It is less than 1/10 000 of the radius of the atom
It is about the same as the radius of the atom
markScheme: 1 mark: It is less than 1/10 000 of the radius of the atom
questions.explanation: The nucleus radius is less than 1/10 000 of the atomic radius. Diagrams exaggerate the nucleus, which is why students often pick a larger fraction.

questions.question: An electron in an atom moves to an energy level further from the nucleus. What must have happened?
markScheme: 1 mark: The atom absorbed electromagnetic radiation
questions.explanation: Moving further from the nucleus means moving to a higher energy level, which needs energy. The energy comes from absorbing electromagnetic radiation. Emission happens when the electron moves closer.

questions.question: What is most of the volume of an atom made of?
markScheme: 1 mark: Empty space
questions.explanation: The nucleus is tiny and electrons are tiny particles too, so most of the atom is empty space between them.

questions.question: The radius of an atom is 1 × 10⁻¹⁰ m. Which value could be the radius of its nucleus?
markScheme: 1 mark: 1 × 10⁻¹⁵ m
questions.explanation: The nucleus radius must be less than 1/10 000 of 1 × 10⁻¹⁰ m, which is 1 × 10⁻¹⁴ m. Only 1 × 10⁻¹⁵ m is smaller than this. 1 × 10⁻¹² m is 1/100 of the atom, far too big.

questions.question:
The radius of an atom is 1.0 × 10⁻¹⁰ m. The radius of its nucleus is 1/10 000 of this.
Calculate the radius of the nucleus in metres.
markScheme: 1 mark: radius = 1.0 × 10⁻¹⁰ ÷ 10 000
1 mark: 1.0 × 10⁻¹⁴ m
questions.explanation: Divide by 10 000 (10⁴): 10⁻¹⁰ ÷ 10⁴ = 10⁻¹⁴. Multiplying instead gives 10⁻⁶ m, which would be bigger than the atom.

questions.question:
A nucleus has a radius of 2 × 10⁻¹⁵ m. The atom has a radius of 1 × 10⁻¹⁰ m.
Calculate how many times larger the radius of the atom is than the radius of the nucleus.
markScheme: 1 mark: ratio = 1 × 10⁻¹⁰ ÷ 2 × 10⁻¹⁵
questions.explanation: 1 × 10⁻¹⁰ ÷ 2 × 10⁻¹⁵ = 0.5 × 10⁵ = 5 × 10⁴. This fits the rule that the nucleus is less than 1/10 000 of the atom.

questions.question:
In a model of an atom, the nucleus is a marble of radius 0.5 cm. In the model the atom radius is 10 000 times the nucleus radius.
Calculate the radius of the model atom in metres.
questions.explanation: 0.5 cm × 10 000 = 5000 cm. There are 100 cm in a metre, so 5000 cm = 50 m. This shows how much empty space an atom contains.

questions.question:
A gold atom has a radius of 1.4 × 10⁻¹⁰ m. Its nucleus has a radius of 7.0 × 10⁻¹⁵ m.
Calculate the ratio radius of atom : radius of nucleus. Give your answer as a single number.
Write the atomic radius 1 × 10⁻¹⁰ m in nanometres. (1 nm = 1 × 10⁻⁹ m)
markScheme: 1 mark: 0.1 nm
questions.explanation: 1 × 10⁻¹⁰ ÷ 1 × 10⁻⁹ = 1 × 10⁻¹ = 0.1 nm. An atom is one tenth of a nanometre across in radius.

questions.question: Name the two types of particle in the nucleus and state the charge of each.
markScheme: 1 mark: proton, positive
1 mark: neutron, no charge (neutral)
questions.explanation: Protons are positive and neutrons are neutral. Electrons are not in the nucleus.

questions.question: State where the electrons are found in an atom.
acceptedAnswers: around the nucleus at different distances
markScheme: 1 mark: in energy levels (shells) at different distances from the nucleus
questions.explanation: Electrons are outside the nucleus, arranged in energy levels at fixed distances from it.

questions.question: State the charge of an electron.
markScheme: 1 mark: negative
questions.explanation: Electrons are negatively charged. Their charge is equal in size but opposite to that of a proton.

questions.question: Explain why the nucleus contains almost all of the mass of an atom even though it is so small.
acceptedAnswers: protons and neutrons much heavier than electrons
markScheme: 1 mark: the nucleus contains the protons and neutrons
1 mark: protons and neutrons have much greater mass than electrons (electrons have a very small mass)
questions.explanation: Mass depends on the particles, not the volume. The heavy particles (protons and neutrons) are all packed into the nucleus.

questions.question: Describe what happens to an electron in an atom when the atom absorbs electromagnetic radiation.
markScheme: 1 mark: the electron gains energy
1 mark: it moves to a higher energy level / further from the nucleus
questions.explanation: Absorbed radiation gives the electron energy, so it moves out to a level further from the nucleus.

questions.question: Describe how an atom emits electromagnetic radiation.
acceptedAnswers: electron moves to lower energy level
markScheme: 1 mark: an electron moves from a higher energy level to a lower energy level / closer to the nucleus
1 mark: the energy lost is emitted as electromagnetic radiation
questions.explanation: When an electron drops to a level closer to the nucleus it loses energy, and that energy is carried away as electromagnetic radiation.

questions.question:
A student says: "An atom is solid all the way through, like a tiny ball bearing."
Use ideas about the structure of the atom to explain why the student is wrong.
acceptedAnswers: electrons at a distance from nucleus
markScheme: 1 mark: the nucleus is very small (radius less than 1/10 000 of the atom)
1 mark: electrons are at relatively large distances from the nucleus
1 mark: so most of the atom is empty space
questions.explanation: The mass is concentrated in a tiny nucleus with electrons far away, so most of the volume is empty space rather than solid material.

questions.question: Explain why a hydrogen atom can only absorb electromagnetic radiation of certain particular energies.
acceptedAnswers: electron must move exactly between levels
markScheme: 1 mark: electrons can only exist in energy levels at particular (fixed) distances from the nucleus
1 mark: so only radiation with energy equal to the difference between two energy levels can be absorbed
questions.explanation: Because the energy levels are fixed, an electron can only jump between them. The energy absorbed must match the gap between two levels exactly.

questions.question: Compare the mass and charge of a proton and an electron.
markScheme: 1 mark: a proton has a much greater mass than an electron
1 mark: a proton is positive and an electron is negative (equal and opposite charge)
questions.explanation: Compare means giving a similarity or difference for each property. The charges are equal in size but opposite in sign, while the masses are very different.

questions.question: Which statement about the electrons in an atom is correct?
options: They are all at the same distance from the nucleus
They are arranged at different distances from the nucleus
They are found inside the nucleus
markScheme: 1 mark: They are arranged at different distances from the nucleus
questions.explanation: Electrons are found in energy levels at different distances from the nucleus. They are negative and outside the nucleus.

questions.question: An electron moves from energy level 3 to energy level 1 in an atom. Which statement is correct?
options: The atom absorbs radiation and the electron moves further from the nucleus
The atom absorbs radiation and the electron moves closer to the nucleus
The atom emits radiation and the electron moves further from the nucleus
The atom emits radiation and the electron moves closer to the nucleus
markScheme: 1 mark: The atom emits radiation and the electron moves closer to the nucleus
questions.explanation: Level 1 is closest to the nucleus and lowest in energy. Dropping from level 3 to level 1 releases energy, which is emitted as electromagnetic radiation.

questions.question: Describe the structure of an atom. Include the particles it contains, where they are found, their charges and the relative size of the nucleus.
markScheme: Indicative content: nucleus at the centre; contains protons (positive) and neutrons (no charge); nucleus is positive overall; electrons (negative) are outside the nucleus in energy levels at different distances; atom radius about 1 × 10⁻¹⁰ m; nucleus radius less than 1/10 000 of the atom; almost all the mass in the nucleus; most of the atom is empty space.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): a clear, detailed description covering particles, locations, charges and relative size.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): some correct statements about particles or locations, with little detail on charge or size.
0 marks: no relevant content.
questions.explanation: A full answer covers what, where, charge and size. Quoting the two size values gains credit.

questions.question:
Scientists say that "an atom is mostly empty space but almost all of its mass is in one tiny place".
Explain this statement and describe how electrons in an atom can absorb and emit electromagnetic radiation.
markScheme: Indicative content: atom radius about 1 × 10⁻¹⁰ m; nucleus radius less than 1/10 000 of atom; nucleus contains protons and neutrons which have much more mass than electrons; so nearly all mass is in the nucleus; electrons are tiny and spread at different distances in energy levels; so most of the volume is empty space; electrons absorb EM radiation and move to higher energy levels further from the nucleus; electrons emit EM radiation when they fall to lower energy levels closer to the nucleus; only particular energies because the levels are at fixed distances.
Level 3 (5 to 6 marks): a detailed, logically linked explanation of both mass concentration and empty space, plus a correct description of absorption and emission linked to energy levels.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): explains one part well or both parts with some gaps in reasoning.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): simple relevant statements with little linking.
0 marks: no relevant content.
questions.explanation: Link each idea: small nucleus plus heavy particles explains the mass; tiny electrons at a distance explain the empty space; moving between levels explains absorption and emission.
